old_problem: The active review kept a standard read-only kernel-log check pending for a project allowlist and start marker. Linux defines severity and time-window filtering, and the source's authoritative criterion is simply absence of GPU errors. Runtime access and timestamps can be detected rather than decided by an engineer.
disposition_reason: The util-linux dmesg interface provides decoded severity, raw/ISO timestamps and since/until selection, while Linux AMDGPU documentation establishes dmesg as primary driver evidence. The review can use an immutable full capture plus a derived MI350/amdgpu error view and treat any emerg/alert/crit/err record in the declared window as FAIL evidence. Warnings remain visible for engineer disposition but are not silently converted to errors. ED-17 forbids the source's log clearing; no project-specific core semantics remain.

test_case.test_name: Immutable MI350/amdgpu kernel error review for the declared test window
test_case.purpose: Prove the preserved kernel message buffer contains no MI350/amdgpu error-severity event in the selected test window while retaining raw context for audit.
required_package: Standard util-linux `dmesg` or systemd `journalctl -k` with read permission
Detected boot ID, kernel/AMDGPU/ROCm versions and stable GPU UUID/BDF inventory
Explicit test start/end timestamps or the current-boot window when this is a standalone health check
test_case.test_command: Record boot ID, versions, GPU inventory and test-window timestamps. Capture `dmesg --kernel --decode --time-format iso --time-format raw` with stderr and actual status into a new immutable file; hash it. From that preserved copy derive (1) every case-insensitive `MI350|amdgpu` line with surrounding context and (2) all decoded `emerg|alert|crit|err` records in the window, correlating resets, faults, RAS/XGMI/PCIe and GPU identities. If dmesg is restricted, use authorized `journalctl -k --boot=0 --since <start> --until <end>` and preserve the query/status; never clear the ring or journal.
test_case.expected_result: The command succeeds with a complete, timestamped current-boot/window capture. No MI350/amdgpu-related emerg, alert, critical or error record, GPU reset/loss, page fault, RAS/XGMI/PCIe failure or initialization failure occurs in the declared window; any warning is preserved with context for explicit disposition.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires readable non-truncated raw evidence, command status 0, correct boot/window correlation and zero relevant error-severity or enumerated GPU-failure event. Permission denial, overwritten/truncated buffer, missing timestamps or a grep pipeline whose no-output status is ambiguous is INCONCLUSIVE, not PASS.
safety_gate: Read only; do not use `dmesg -C`, `--clear`, SEL clear or journal vacuuming
Use approved secure access without embedded passwords or disabled host verification
Preserve raw output before filtering and record stderr/exit status
Stop interpretation on privilege, boot-ID, timestamp, truncation or GPU-identity ambiguity; never auto-retry
expected_evidence: Boot ID, kernel/AMDGPU/ROCm versions and GPU UUID/BDF map
Exact command, access identity, start/end time, stdout/stderr and process status
MI350/amdgpu contextual view and severity-based error view with timestamp correlation
Warning disposition, post-capture integrity and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: No state change is expected. On an access or evidence failure, preserve stderr/status and request read permission or persistent journal evidence; do not clear logs, reboot, modify kernel settings or rerun automatically.
